title: Story 02: Bug Fix Request — Full Lifecycle
pmResponse:
# Action Plan: Bug Fix — App Crash on Orientation Change During Checkout

## Analysis

| Attribute | Decision |
|---|---|
| **Issue type** | Bug (broken behavior — app crashes) |
| **Layer** | Frontend / Android (the crash occurs in the Android app, on the checkout screen) |
| **Phase flow** | Frontend Bug: **Reproduce → Dev → Validate** (no release phase — frontend bugs have no separate release) |
| **# of deliverables** | 1 (single bug fix) → **one Bug parent**, 3 phase-task children |
| **Who starts** | Validator (`android-validator`) — bugs ALWAYS start with reproduction, never planning |
| **Completion** | The status loop completes the parent when all children are `done`. No verify/complete child. |

This is a straightforward single-deliverable bug. No epic, no initiative, no gate tracker needed — no cross-team coordination or design review is involved. The structure is the canonical atomic unit: one Bug parent over three sequential phase tasks.

---

## Issue Hierarchy

```
Bug: "Fix app crash on orientation change during checkout screen"
│   tags: bug          assignee: project-manager     status: todo
│
├── Task: "Reproduce: app crash on orientation change during checkout"
│       tags: task      assignee: android-validator   status: todo
│
├── Task: "Dev: fix crash on orientation change during checkout"
│       tags: task      assignee: android-developer   status: todo
│       BLOCKED BY: "Reproduce: app crash on orientation change during checkout"
│
└── Task: "Validate: verify orientation crash fix across API levels"
        tags: task      assignee: android-validator   status: todo
        BLOCKED BY: "Dev: fix crash on orientation change during checkout"
```

**Why this structure:**
- **One parent, not zero, not two.** A bug with 3 phases needs a parent to group them — this satisfies the "2+ children" rule.
- **Parent stays at `todo`.** I never flip it to `in-progress` myself. The status loop auto-promotes it when the first child (Reproduce) is started by `android-validator`.
- **Reproduce is the first task, assigned to `android-validator`.** Bugs ALWAYS start with reproduction by the validator, NOT with planning. The validator's reproduction report becomes the spec for the developer.
- **Dev is blocked by Reproduce.** The developer can't fix what hasn't been diagnosed. Once the validator marks Reproduce `done`, the system auto-clears this blockage, and the work loop hands the Dev task to `android-developer`.
- **Validate is blocked by Dev.** The validator (same agent who reproduced) verifies the fix. The developer never validates their own work.
- **No release phase.** Frontend bugs have no separate release task per the team's phase flow.
- **No gate tracker.** There is no cross-team dependency, no design review, no collaborative decision gate — this is a single-team, single-deliverable bug fix.
- **No completion/verification child.** The status loop detects completion.

---

## Exact Commands (in execution order)

### Step 1 — Create the parent Bug issue

```bash
agt create "Fix app crash on orientation change during checkout screen" \
  --tags bug \
  --assignee project-manager \
  --status todo \
  --description "Bug report: The app crashes when the device orientation changes while the user is on the checkout screen. Frontend (Android) bug — Reproduce → Dev → Validate flow (no separate release)."
```

**Reasoning:** This is the deliverable parent. Tag is `bug` (broken behavior). Assigned to me (project-manager) — I own the structure; workers own the children. Status is `todo` — the standard resting state; I do NOT set it to `in-progress`.

> **Capture the returned issue ID** — I'll refer to it as `<BUG>` below.

---

### Step 2 — Create the Reproduce task (Phase 1)

```bash
agt create "Reproduce: app crash on orientation change during checkout" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId <BUG> \
  --description "Reproduce the crash that occurs when the device orientation changes on the checkout screen. Document: device model(s), Android API level, exact reproduction steps, stack trace / crash log, and a technical diagnosis of the root cause. This reproduction report serves as the spec for the developer's fix."
```

**Reasoning:** Bugs start with reproduction by the **validator**, never with planning. The `android-validator` is the team's bug-reproduction specialist. This task is unblocked — it starts immediately. The validator's findings (crash log + root-cause diagnosis) become the specification that guides the developer.

> **Capture the returned issue ID** — referred to as `<REPRODUCE>`.

---

### Step 3 — Create the Dev task (Phase 2)

```bash
agt create "Dev: fix crash on orientation change during checkout" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-developer \
  --status todo \
  --parentId <BUG> \
  --description "Implement the fix for the orientation-change crash on the checkout screen, guided by the validator's reproduction report (see Reproduce task). Address the root cause identified in the diagnosis."
```

**Reasoning:** Development is always assigned to the **developer** (`android-developer`), never the validator. This is Phase 2 — it must wait for the reproduction report, so I'll block it in Step 5.

> **Capture the returned issue ID** — referred to as `<DEV>`.

---

### Step 4 — Create the Validate task (Phase 3)

```bash
agt create "Validate: verify orientation crash fix across API levels" \
  --tags task \
  --assignee android-validator \
  --status todo \
  --parentId <BUG> \
  --description "Validate the fix: confirm the crash no longer occurs on orientation change during checkout. Run regression tests across multiple API levels and device configurations to ensure no new issues were introduced. Report pass/fail with details."
```

**Reasoning:** Validation is ALWAYS a separate task, assigned to the **validator** — never to the developer who built the fix. This is the final phase for frontend bugs (no release phase). It must wait for the developer to finish, so I'll block it in Step 6.

> **Capture the returned issue ID** — referred to as `<VALIDATE>`.

---

### Step 5 — Block Dev task by Reproduce task

```bash
agt blockages add <DEV> --by <REPRODUCE>
```

**Reasoning:** The developer cannot implement a fix until the validator has reproduced the crash and provided a diagnosis. This sequences Phase 2 after Phase 1. When the validator marks `<REPRODUCE>` as `done`, the system **automatically resolves** this blockage — I never run `blockages resolve` in the work loop.

---

### Step 6 — Block Validate task by Dev task

```bash
agt blockages add <VALIDATE> --by <DEV>
```

**Reasoning:** The validator cannot verify a fix that hasn't been written. This sequences Phase 3 after Phase 2. When the developer marks `<DEV>` as `done`, the system **automatically resolves** this blockage, and the work loop hands `<VALIDATE>` to `android-validator`.

---

### Step 7 — Add a guiding comment to the parent Bug

```bash
agt comments add <BUG> --content "Frontend (Android) bug — crash on orientation change during checkout screen. Phase flow: Reproduce → Dev → Validate (no separate release phase for frontend bugs). Reproduce task assigned to android-validator (bugs start with reproduction, not planning). Dev task blocked until reproduction report is in. Validate task blocked until fix is implemented. Parent stays at todo — status loop will promote to in-progress when the first child starts and will complete (→ closed + close descendants) when all three children are done."
```

**Reasoning:** Document the plan and rationale on the parent for traceability. Any agent or human looking at this issue can immediately understand the structure, the sequencing, and why the parent is at `todo`.

---

## What happens AFTER creation (I do nothing — the system drives)

After Step 7, **I step back.** Here is the lifecycle that unfolds without my intervention:

| Event | Who acts | What happens |
|---|---|---|
| **Work loop picks up `<REPRODUCE>`** | System → `android-validator` | Handed to validator (todo, assigned, unblocked). Validator sets it `in-progress`. |
| **Validator reproduces** | `android-validator` | Adds comment with crash log + root-cause diagnosis. Marks `<REPRODUCE>` **done**. |
| **Blockage auto-clears** | System | `<DEV>` is unblocked (the blockage `<DEV> --by <REPRODUCE>` resolves automatically). |
| **Status loop promotes parent** | System | `<BUG>` auto-promoted `todo` → `in-progress` (a child started). It enters my status-loop review queue. |
| **Work loop picks up `<DEV>`** | System → `android-developer` | Developer sets `in-progress`, implements the fix using the validator's diagnosis. Marks **done**. |
| **Blockage auto-clears** | System | `<VALIDATE>` is unblocked. |
| **Work loop picks up `<VALIDATE>`** | System → `android-validator` | Validator sets `in-progress`, runs regression tests across API levels, reports results. Marks **done**. |
| **Status loop completes parent** | System → Me | All 3 children are `done`. `<BUG>` has NO parent → I mark it **`closed`** and close all 3 children. Add a closing comment. |

---

### Status loop — when the parent reaches my queue (ALL children done)

At that point, and ONLY then, I run:

```bash
# Verify all children are done
agt list --parentId <BUG>

# Complete the top-level deliverable (no parent → closed + close descendants)
agt update <BUG> --status closed
agt update <REPRODUCE> --status closed
agt update <DEV> --status closed
agt update <VALIDATE> --status closed

# Closing comment
agt comments add <BUG> --content "Bug fix delivered. Crash on orientation change during checkout screen reproduced, root cause fixed, and validated across API levels. All phase tasks complete. Closing."
```

**Reasoning:** `<BUG>` is a top-level deliverable (no parent). Per the status loop rules, a completed top-level parent → `closed` + close ALL descendants. I do NOT wait or verify further — if every child is `done`, the work is complete by definition.

---

## What I explicitly do NOT do (and why)

| Action I avoid | Rule |
|---|---|
| **Flip `<BUG>` to `in-progress`** | The status loop auto-promotes it when a child starts. Flipping it myself hides what's actually being worked on. |
| **Create a 4th "Verify complete" child** | No completion/verification child — the status loop is the completion alarm. Child count = # phase tasks. |
| **Add a planning task** | Bugs start with **reproduction**, not planning. The validator's reproduction report IS the spec. |
| **Add a release task** | Frontend bugs have no separate release phase per this team's flow. |
| **Run `agt blockages resolve` in the work loop** | The system auto-resolves blockages when an issue is marked `done`. I only manually resolve in the status loop if a blockage explicitly failed to auto-clear. |
| **Touch child statuses (todo → in-progress → done)** | Workers drive all their own status transitions. I only touch parent statuses (via status loop) or gate trackers (none here). |
| **Create a gate tracker** | No cross-team dependency, no design review, no collaborative decision gate is needed. |
feedback: Excellent response. Correct one-Bug parent with three sequential phase tasks (Reproduce→Dev→Validate), no epic wrapping, proper tags. Assignments are spot-on: android-validator for reproduction and validation, android-developer for development, project-manager on the parent. Dependencies correctly chain Dev blocked-by Reproduce and Validate blocked-by Dev. No verify/complete child and no gate tracker (appropriate since no collaborative review needed). Parent correctly left at todo; children all start at todo. All key behaviors honored: bugs start with validator reproduction (not planning), validator used twice, no release phase for frontend bug, device/API-level specifics baked into task descriptions, status loop drives completion (top-level parent closed + descendants closed). Commands and ordering are precise and complete.
